newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower again.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to off again Friday in moderate activity, still weighed down by ample supply despite the prospect that stocks will be trimmed some by the onset of an eastern cold wave.
"It's getting cold, but the whole (resid) complex looks terrible. There's just too many barrels sitting around," said one cash trader.

U.S. Gulf one percent slipped a quarter to $16.75 a barrel, with three percent off slightly to $15.25-15.50. Traders said reports an eight gravity February one percent cargo sold at just over $17 (delivered Fla.) pressured the market.
Traders said a Florida utility awarded its tender for 2.2 percent at $16.85 and 1.8 percent at $17.10, both delivered to Jacksonville.
In New York Harbor, prices were relatively stable but sentiment remained mostly bearish because of oversupply.
NYH physical one percent was still talked at about $17.75, with 2.2 percent also unchanged at about $17, traders said.
The onset Friday of colder weather in New York kept weekend gas prices steady at about $6.00/mmBtu. NYH one percent resid remained at a $2.82/mmBtu equivalent.
